title: Multi-phase agent-driven paper processing and claim projection environment

environment.label: Agent Phases
environment.description: The environment organizes agent activity into distinct phases: fetched, judged, projected, read, escalated, among others.

environment.label: External Data Sources
environment.description: External repositories including huggingface, github, zenodo, openalex, openclaw, and wikipedia provide items (metadata or records) via designated access methods.

environment.label: Source Identifier Formats
environment.description: Sources are identified with prefixes like 'zenodo:', 'huggingface:', and 'arxiv:'. Other formats are not recognized by the system.

environment.label: Language Models
environment.description: The environment includes specific language models: ibm-granite/granite-4.1-8b-20260429 and deepseek-v4-pro. These models have internal gates that can filter outputs.

environment.label: Paper Queue
environment.description: During the read phase, papers to be processed are held in a queue.

environment.label: Decision Authority Layer
environment.description: A distinct decision authority (Layer 9) has final say over claims, rejecting proposals deemed insufficient or incorrect.

inference.label: Partial Source Return
inference.description: If a source cannot provide the full requested quantity of items, it returns fewer items, causing a shortfall in the fetch.

inference.label: Source Access Failure
inference.description: Rate limits, authentication requirements, or permission errors cause fetch requests to fail, preventing item retrieval from that source.

inference.label: Abstract Retrieval Dependency
inference.description: Accurate paper relevance assessment requires the paper's abstract; if abstract retrieval fails or times out, automated relevance verification is blocked.

inference.label: Identifier Parsing Failure
inference.description: If a source identifier does not match expected prefix formats, the Granite model fails to parse it, resulting in zero proposal generation.

inference.label: Model Gate Filtering
inference.description: The Granite model's internal gate can filter out all generated candidates, causing an empty projection output.

inference.label: Resource Intensity of Reading
inference.description: Reading full text of papers consumes significant computational resources, potentially leading to bottlenecks.

inference.label: Downstream Integration Requirement
inference.description: Text extracted during the read phase is not automatically consumed; downstream modules must be integrated, otherwise reading yields zero utility.

inference.label: Layer 9 Rejection Resets Proposal Cycle
inference.description: When Layer 9 rejects all proposed claims as insufficient or incorrect, the proposal cycle must be repeated.

constraints.label: Title-Only Relevance Insufficiency
constraints.description: Paper relevance cannot be accurately determined from title alone; abstract content is necessary for reliable assessment.

constraints.label: Source Identifier Format Requirement
constraints.description: Source identifiers must conform to recognized prefixes (e.g., zenodo:, huggingface:, arxiv:); other formats are invalid and cause parsing failures.

constraints.label: Rate and Permission Limits
constraints.description: External sources enforce rate limits and authentication requirements; requests that exceed these limits or lack proper credentials fail.

constraints.label: Model Proposals Not Authoritative
constraints.description: Claims proposed by language models in the projected or escalated phases are candidates only; they do not have decision authority, which rests with Layer 9.

body:
## Environment

The agent operates in a multi-phase pipeline (fetched, judged, projected, read, escalated) interacting with external repositories: huggingface, github, zenodo, openalex, openclaw, and wikipedia. Each source provides items via specific access methods and is identified by prefixes (zenodo:, huggingface:, arxiv:). Two language models, ibm-granite/granite-4.1-8b-20260429 and deepseek-v4-pro, are available for proposal generation, each with internal output filtering. A queue holds papers during the read phase, and a separate authority (Layer 9) controls final claim decisions.

## Inference Rules

- Sources may return fewer items than requested, causing shortfalls.
- Rate limits, missing authentication, or permission errors cause fetch failures.
- Relevance assessment depends on abstract availability; retrieval failures block it.
- Misformatted source identifiers cause Granite model to produce no proposals.
- The Granite model’s gate can filter all candidates, yielding an empty projection.
- Full-text reading is resource‑intensive and useless unless downstream modules are integrated.
- Layer 9 rejection of all proposed claims necessitates a new proposal cycle.

## Constraints

- Title alone is insufficient for relevance; abstract content is mandatory.
- Source identifiers must use recognized prefixes; others are invalid.
- External sources enforce rate and permission boundaries; exceeding them causes failures.
- Language model outputs are non‑authoritative; only Layer 9 can finalize claims.
